title: ATOMSTACK Laser Engravers: A10, A20, A40 and A70
metaDescription: ATOMSTACK's laser engravers compared by power, area and price: the A10 Pro V2 10W, A20 Pro V2 20W, A40 Pro V2 48W and the 70W A70 MAX, from $252.73 to $1875.07.
author: ByteBuy Team

sections.content: ATOMSTACK builds its range around power: 10W, 20W, 48W and 70W, with the model name pointing to the step. The three Pro V2 machines share a 400 mm-class bed and differ mostly in laser output and price, while the A70 MAX is a large-format machine with an 800x850 mm area. This guide compares the four so you can see what each extra watt costs, from $252.73 to $1875.07.

items.label: A10 Pro V2 10W ($252.73)
items.value: 410x380 mm area, 400 mm/s, 0.01 mm precision, 0.06x0.08 mm spot

items.label: A20 Pro V2 20W ($396.20)
items.value: 400x365 mm area, 400 mm/s, 0.01 mm precision, 0.08x0.1 mm spot

items.label: A40 Pro V2 48W ($999)
items.value: 395x385 mm area, 500 mm/s, auto air assist, listing states 25 mm paulownia or 9 mm MDF in one pass

items.label: A70 MAX 70W ($1875.07)
items.value: 800x850 mm area, 400 mm/s, 0.02 mm precision, auto focus, offline touchscreen, intelligent air assist, dual-rail motion, flame detection, power-loss resume

pros: The A10 Pro V2 has the finest spot of the three Pro V2 models (0.06x0.08 mm) and the lowest price, $252.73
The A20 Pro V2 doubles the stated power for about $143 more and keeps the same bed class
The A40 Pro V2 adds auto air assist and a stated cutting capacity of 25 mm paulownia in one pass
The A70 MAX has a much larger 800x850 mm area plus auto focus and a touchscreen
The A70 MAX lists flame detection and power-loss resume, two features that matter on long jobs
cons: Moving from the A20 to the A40 costs over $600 for the same bed size, so you pay for power, not area
The A70 MAX costs $1875.07 and needs a large workspace, a dedicated table and good ventilation
The A10 and A20 listings do not mention air assist, so check the product page if you plan to cut
A larger spot (0.08x0.1 mm on the A20 and A40) means slightly less fine detail than the A10
Stated cutting depths are best cases and depend on material and passes

items.question: Which ATOMSTACK should I buy first?
items.answer: The A10 Pro V2 is the sensible start if you mostly engrave. Choose the A20 if you want to cut wood and acrylic with fewer passes. The A40 and A70 are for people who cut regularly or work at larger scale.

items.question: Is the A70 MAX overkill?
items.answer: For a home hobbyist, usually yes. Its value is the 800x850 mm bed and the safety and convenience features. It suits a small workshop or business.

items.question: What are laser beds for?
items.answer: A honeycomb bed lifts the workpiece and lets smoke and heat escape, which gives cleaner cuts. ATOMSTACK sells the F2N (300x300 mm, $36.41) and F4N (400x400 mm, $55.17), which suit the 400 mm-class machines.

items.question: Do the lasers need air assist?
items.answer: For cutting, air assist helps keep the cut clean and reduces flare-ups. The A40 Pro V2 and A70 MAX list it, so check the product page for the A10 and A20 if you plan to cut.

items.question: What safety gear do I need?
items.answer: Laser-rated eye protection, ventilation or an extractor, and a fire extinguisher nearby. Never leave a running machine unattended, whatever safety features it lists.

sections.content: Pick the power to match the work: the A10 for engraving on a budget, the A20 for cutting with a margin, the A40 for fast thick cuts and the A70 MAX for large projects. Beds like the F4N are a cheap add-on that improves cut quality on any of the 400 mm machines.
